description: The actual Chrome-to-Marvain journey; extend only when a feature has a user acceptance receipt.

steps: Deploy the selected tagged Hub to the existing Ohio stack through Marvain CLI.
Sign in through Marvain Cognito Hosted UI using the allowed Google account.
Select the existing INITagent and laptop space, with the owner linked to John.
Prepare the private retain-all browser binding and canonical scene/session using the owning browser-activation operation.
Activate the AWS responder and use its owning service result.
Open Live Session in Chrome and select laptop.
Click Join, allow microphone access, and say Hello Marvain.
Hear a spoken Marvain response, then click Leave.

proven_features.acceptance: this works great. however, the leave and join processes are really slow
steps: Join the existing laptop space and speak a distinctive recall marker.
Click Leave, then Join to create a different session.
Ask for the marker without repeating the answer.
Hear the correct marker recalled, confirmed by the human.
proven_features.execution: attended browser interaction; automated test source written, not run

steps: Join a new session after loading the released Live Session page.
Enable Camera and confirm the live preview stays visible.
Ask aloud what Marvain can see; confirm its description matches visible content.
Change the view and ask again; confirm it describes the new frame.
Disable Camera and ask again; confirm it reports that the camera is off.
acceptance: Correctly reports camera off; I’ve left
proven_features.execution: attended browser interaction; automated test source written, not run

steps: Use the existing approved face reference and active consent.
Join the laptop space with Turn microphone on when joining unchecked.
Type a greeting and hear the reply while Mic Off remains enabled.
Enable Camera with the enrolled face alone in view.
Type Recognize my face from the camera using the approved face reference.
Observe Fresh face comparison: John in the lifecycle events and hear the matching reply.
